open_problems: Both knees straddle the XL330's own 70 degC Temperature Limit(31) at the measured walking duty. This is the single most consequential thermal result: if the real emissivity and mount blockage land on the bad side, the servo latches Overheating Error (Shutdown(63) Bit 2) mid-walk. One servo step test settles it and nothing else will.

The MJCF's actuator forcerange is +/-0.96 N.m against the vendor's 0.60 N.m stall torque at 6.0 V — the simulation is allowed 1.6x more torque than the real part can make. Lane F2 already grades 12 joints over the 6.0 V stall row in push cells. Every thermal number here is computed at the measured torques regardless, but a policy retrained inside the real limit would change the duty.

The compute's failing thermal leg is die-to-skin and there is no conduction path in the design at all: 194.171 cm3 of still air, no vent, no fan, no heatsink between a 95 degC die and a shell the external solution puts in the high twenties. This is a mechanical design item (a pad or bracket from the SoC to the shell), not an electronics one, and no lane currently owns it.

The whole 14-hinge tolerance stack rests on a published service tolerance because print_fits.json is empty. Until one coupon is printed and measured, every fit number in this repo is a bound, not a value — and the bound says a Ø16 printed bearing seat is coarser than IT15, which cannot be right for a product that works.

Seven joints seat a 4.0 mm ring on a 1.95 mm boss. The consequence is now quantified — the bearing leaves 27.1497 deg of cocking freedom at FDM-A and therefore contributes almost nothing to holding the joint's angle — so the flange is doing all the work and its form tolerance is the one thing nobody has measured.

lane: F2 — MuJoCo gait robustness + battery runtime
open_problems: The simulated gait exceeds the XL330-M288-T's published stall torque on EVERY 5 deg slope and at every command >= 0.60 m/s. Whether the physical robot can walk a 5 deg slope at all is now an open product question: the sim asks right_hip_pitch for 0.8022 N.m and the servo's ceiling is 0.60 N.m at 6.0 V. Lane H should add a slope-walk acceptance test; lane G should state the slope limit in the playbook.

Pollen's MJCF permits +/-0.96 N.m per joint, 1.60x the highest published stall row. Any conclusion drawn from a cell where the actuator saturates (every push cell, every sit-stand cell) is the simulation's ceiling, not a servo capability. The model would be more faithful with forcerange set to the vendor row for the pack voltage actually used — but no vendor figure exists above 6.0 V and the robot runs the servos at 6.6-8.2 V, so that clamp cannot be set from evidence today.

The walking policy does not hold a straight line: net yaw drift reaches -186.608 deg over 12 s at vx 0.80 (-36.37 deg per metre of ground track), and the forward tracking ratio (mean path speed / commanded vx) sits between 0.514 and 0.637 in every moving level-ground cell. A walk acceptance test that measures straight-line displacement will understate distance and will fail a heading criterion the policy was never trained to meet.

stand_from_FOLD does not recover: the robot stays down with left_hip_pitch pinned at the 0.9600 N.m MJCF ceiling for the whole attempt. Either the FOLD keyframe is outside the stand policy's basin or the actuator model is the binding constraint — the two are not separable while that ceiling sits above the vendor's stall row.
